name: Iodamoeba buetschlii

taxonomy.rank_note: Reference groups can include multiple species. Protozoan higher-rank systems differ; the lineage is provided without forcing every clade into a class rank.

morphology: Cyst: approximately 5–20 µm, variable outline, usually one nucleus and a glycogen vacuole that becomes dark brown with iodine.
Trophozoites have a large karyosome and lack the uniform peripheral chromatin of Entamoeba.

transmission.detail: Ingested cysts establish colonization; trophozoites multiply in the intestine and encyst before shedding.

life_cycle.detail: Ingested cysts establish colonization; trophozoites multiply in the intestine and encyst before shedding.

hosts: Humans are the principal clinical host; no intermediate host.
distribution: Worldwide, including Southeast Asia; findings indicate fecal exposure.
clinical_significance: Generally considered nonpathogenic. Correct identification helps avoid attributing symptoms to a harmless colonizer.
diagnostics: Iodine aids cyst assessment; permanent stained smears near 1000× resolve nuclei.
Interpret glycogen in iodine mounts and chromatin in permanent stains separately.
differential_diagnosis: Immature or degraded amoebae may resemble the E. histolytica complex. Combine calibrated size, mature nuclear count and chromatin pattern.
review_status: Source-compiled educational content; not independently clinically validated

annotation_guidance: Record specimen, stage, stain, objective/total magnification, pixel calibration, source image and reviewer certainty.
Native crops of 200–650 pixels do not determine biological size. Retain µm-per-pixel calibration before resizing.
Split training, validation and test data by patient/specimen; keep related crops in the same split.
Keep damaged or ambiguous objects uncertain. Molecular confirmation of a mixed specimen does not assign every pictured object a species.
